message.content: Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra. Their most recent common ancestor lies in the clade **Laurasiatheria**, a group of placental mammals that split from other mammalian lineages roughly 90 million years ago. Thus, the common ancestor of lion and zebra is a mammal from the Laurasiatheria clade that lived around that time.
